old: The restarts are the Cluster Operator finishing the disk resize, not the retention edit. After size went from 1000Gi to 2000Gi, Kubernetes grew the persistent volumes; kubectl get pv already shows 2000Gi. When that resize completes, the operator restarts every pod that uses the resized volume, and the restart is automatic. Confirm the reason with kubectl -n billing get events --field-selector reportingController=strimzi.io/cluster-operator. FileSystemResizeNeeded means the filesystem grew and a restart was required to apply it. ConfigChangeRequiresRestart is a different reason, used when a broker setting cannot be applied live. log.retention.hours is a default topic configuration brokers update without a restart, so that edit did not roll the pods. ManualRollingUpdate would mean a roll annotation, PodForceRestartOnError an error restart, and CaCertRenewed or KafkaCertificatesChanged a certificate roll. Raising size does not drop data. Do not delete the PVCs. Do not set size back to 1000Gi: decreasing a persistent volume is not supported. If 72 hours was a mistake, set log.retention.hours back to 168; that change is dynamic.

old: Compaction never rewrites the active segment, and each partition still has only that one open segment (segment.bytes is 1 GiB and the topic writes about 20 MB/day, so it has not rolled). With max.compaction.lag.ms unset, a log that does not exceed min.cleanable.dirty.ratio is also left uncompacted, which is how a low-rate topic stays dirty forever. Set the topic max.compaction.lag.ms (or the broker log.cleaner.max.compaction.lag.ms) so the head becomes eligible after a bounded delay. That deadline is not a hard guarantee; watch uncleanable-partitions-count, max-clean-time-secs and max-compaction-delay-secs. Roll back a topic override with kafka-configs.sh --alter --delete-config max.compaction.lag.ms. Do not switch the topic to delete, and do not raise min.cleanable.dirty.ratio.
new: Compaction never rewrites the active segment, and each partition still has only that one open segment (segment.bytes is 1 GiB, each partition gets about 20 MB/day, and segment.ms is set to 365 days, so it has rolled neither by size nor by time). old: Leave the lag unset and lower segment.bytes so the open segment closes. Closed segments are eligible; the active one is not. Raising the dirty ratio would make a clean less likely.

The directory listing and the 20 MB/day rate are invented. The describe lines follow the dynamic-config layout used in the docs. segment.bytes as a roll control is stated in the tiered-storage quick start comment. Second review: m3c raised to weight 2: the three members are equally correct fixes (a rolled segment is closed, and a closed log is 100 percent dirty, so it exceeds min.cleanable.dirty.ratio); the author's reason for weight 1 does not hold, and the correct_alternative takes m3c.
new: any_of m3a/m3b/m3c: topic lag, broker lag, or rolling the segment. m3c is weight 1 because a roll alone does not bound a log that stays under the dirty ratio; the reference prefers the lag. The directory listing, the 20 MB/day per-partition rate and the 365-day segment.ms override are invented; without the override the 7-day default segment.ms (822fab3d5711a8ea) would have rolled each partition about six times. The describe lines follow the dynamic-config layout used in the docs. segment.bytes as a roll control is stated in the tiered-storage quick start comment. Second review: m3c raised to weight 2: the three members are equally correct fixes (a rolled segment is closed, and a closed log is 100 percent dirty, so it exceeds min.cleanable.dirty.ratio); the author's reason for weight 1 does not hold, and the correct_alternative takes m3c.
